correctness.rationale: Exact continuous/discrete coupon-process coupling, DKW applied to each Gamma jth-arrival empirical CDF followed by an O(sqrt(log N))-index union bound, uniform Poisson local-limit linearization around log N, uniform fourth moments of the exponential maximum, and optional-stopping isometry E[(T/N-C)^2]=H_N/N together prove the stated compact-uniform mean-square approximation. Ordinary Poisson CLT and L2 moment convergence give the other displayed assertions. The standalone checker passes 87 finite assertions; it is not a proof of the infinite theorem.

originality.rationale: The motivating same-model paper arXiv:2606.29635 fixes all album indices and explicitly states it does not cover growing j. Full-text comparison with Ilienko (2026) in the infinite-dimensional product topology and with arXiv:2606.31391 and the accessible earlier sibling work reveals no implication of a uniform log-index Gumbel process; six distinct semantic database queries found no directly covering recorded statement. This remains best-knowledge, provisional historical originality because the general occupancy/empirical-process literature is broad and the 2020 first-sibling paper could not be fully examined (while the 2012 Mahmoud–Smythe primary text was inspected and found noncovering).

value.rationale: The source identifies growing sibling index as an open regime. The window j≈log N is the natural transition from a vanishing fraction of empty places to a macroscopic Gaussian-CDF profile. The theorem provides the full compact-uniform first fluctuation with explicit non-Gaussian Gumbel amplitude and rank-one covariance, which cannot be inferred by substituting a growing index into the published fixed-J limit. It is structurally informative for higher-order and heterogeneous extensions, beyond a pointwise Poisson approximation. Ilienko (2026) treats all fixed ranks in a product topology but still leaves the moving-rank critical-window question distinct.
